transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining the week three sync. um I see most of the usuals on the call. Carlos, Anika, Tobias, Jenna, thank you. we'll try to keep to 45 minutes but we've got a bit to cover.
[00:18] Carlos: yeah thanks, Maya. we've had a couple of bad windows this week — some 5xx spikes when the handshakes hit during our morning ramp.
[00:36] Anika: right, the psks seemed to retry a lot. i caught a few packets that looked like the prehandshake was timing out, maybe 200ms spikes? hard to tell cause our capture had some gaps.
[00:52] Liam: okay that's useful, and thanks for the pcap you uploaded — saw it. initial thought is the AKS egress path plus MTU fragmentation we discussed last week might be amplifying retransmits; the runtime backoff is conservative so it queues, then times out.
[01:10] Tobias: is that on your side or ours? are we misconfiguring the peering ACL?
[01:16] Liam: mostly it's the network path — small MTU (1400) plus intermittent packet loss at the edge. when the KV cache warms up, we see bursty traffic that causes some loss. the runtime's handshake retry multiplies the load.
[01:30] Maya: ok so practical next steps: liam will prepare a canary kernel roll that changes the retry window and tightens early ack behavior; anika will run a controlled stress test to reproduce.
[01:44] Anika: i can run that Thursday afternoon. question tho — what's the expected observable? latency? handshake fails? error codes?
[01:52] Liam: primarily latency tail and handshake error rate (we'll give you exact counters). also we want pcap and the redwood agent logs with debug level for the session id.
[02:04] Carlos: got it. and we're still seeing some odd telemetry gaps — some request id's show up in application logs but not in the redwood agent metrics.
[02:14] Priya: that gap's been on our radar. we've noticed the on-prem collector drops events under memory pressure. the telemetry bundle update will add disk-backed buffering.
[02:26] Jenna: security here — we have a few lawyers asking for KMS integration details and audit log samples. can you share those?
[02:34] Maya: yes, we can. i'll gather the KMS integration docs, example audit logs, and a short SOC2 mapping doc. it won't be the entire attestation but should cover the items your security team asked for.
[02:46] Tobias: perfect, that helps. another thing — cost. the quantized runtime we're testing saved about 22% on token compute in the preliminary run, but we did see a bump in latency. can you share the profile so we can make a call between latency vs cost?
[03:02] Maya: absolutely. i'll send the profile and a simple cost model spreadsheet that shows expected per-1M token delta.
[03:12] Anika: on the canary patch — what is rollback like? we can't risk a long outage.
[03:18] Liam: rollback is one command; i'm preparing a script that will revert to previous kernel and reconverge caches. we'll test it in canary and document the steps. worst case you can roll back within 5 minutes.
[03:30] Carlos: good. are there any behavioral changes we should expect in caching? like cache invalidation or kv key shapes?
[03:36] Liam: no functional changes to cache semantics, mostly timing and backoff tweaks. there is one opt-in path that changes how prefix caching is batched for very long prompts — that will be off by default.
[03:48] Tobias: telemetry again — what metrics are we missing? request latency histogram? pipeline queue depth?
[03:54] Priya: we found we weren't emitting per-route token split and the agent's queue depth metric wasn't present in older agent builds. newer bundle includes route_token_split, agent_queue_depth, and handshake_retry_count.
[04:08] Jenna: on KMS: do we support external HSM or only cloud-managed KMS?
[04:12] Maya: we support both: cloud KMS integration is straightforward, for HSM we have a connector that does key wrapping and attestation. i'll include the connector design and the necessary thumbprint samples.
[04:24] Anika: about the stress test we plan to spike to 5k rps for 10 minutes — do you want a gradual ramp or instant?
[04:32] Liam: gradual ramp over 2 minutes, hold for 10, then decay. that lets us see where queues build. also please include SNMP counters and a pcap.
[04:44] Carlos: one odd failure we saw yesterday was after a long idle period; a couple of requests sketched a 4s cold-start gag, then normal. any idea?
[04:54] Liam: that could be KV cache eviction policy interacting with the runtime's lazy loading. we're adding a small pre-warm ping in the canary to keep critical keys resident.
[05:06] Maya: ok, rolling through schedule — liam will push canary Friday morning (UTC), monitor for 24 hours; anika runs stress Thursday; priya will ship telemetry update by Tuesday; maya to send docs and cost spreadsheet by Monday.
[05:20] Tobias: sounds good. last question: competitors — we ran some side-by-side tests vs Vertex and there was some parity on throughput but your fallback model variant flattened the tail better. is that the built-in fallback policy?
[05:36] Maya: yes, that's the smart routing + fallback. it'll be part of the notes I send. just be aware fallback can increase token costs if it shifts to a larger variant.
[05:48] Carlos: perfect. any blockers from Redwood's side?
[05:52] Liam: none; just timing to prepare the canary package and run internal smoke.
[05:58] Maya: ok i'll recap next steps in the email and attach the deck, the quant profile, and the SOC2 mapping. thanks everyone.
[06:06] Carlos: thanks all.
[06:08] (crosstalk) Jenna: thanks, bye.
[06:12] End of recording.
